Long Beach after the C-17: SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410 and the new rocket factories

For most of a century Long Beach built aircraft, from Douglas airliners to the C-17 airlifter. The former C-17 plant west of Long Beach Airport is now Relativity Space's headquarters, a factory of about a million square feet on 93 acres. Rocket Lab, a Long Beach-based launch company, builds its 3D-printed Rutherford engines and develops the Archimedes engine for its Neutron rocket in a 144,000-square-foot facility that used to be Virgin Orbit's headquarters. Across town, refineries, terminals and ship repair keep the older NDT trades busy. Which certification document applies depends on which side of the city you work.

Launch companies set their own rulebook

New space companies are not classic tier-two aerospace suppliers. Many hold contracts with their customers directly, and they write NDT personnel requirements into their own quality systems, shaped by what their government and commercial customers ask for. Depending on those contracts, the written practice can rest on NAS 410 or, where the contracts allow it, on ASNT SNT-TC-1A with the customer's additions. Printed engine parts, welded tanks and composite structures call for penetrant, ultrasonic and radiographic examination, and the inspector's certification has to fit the contract behind each part. Ask which standard and revision the written practice names before you assume either.

Suppliers to the rocket and aircraft builders

Machine shops, welders and finishers around the airport and in Carson and Torrance that make hardware for launch and aircraft programs usually meet NAS 410 the classic way: a quality clause in the purchase order, passed down from the customer. Once that clause is in force the shop needs a Responsible Level 3 (RL3) designated in writing, formal documented training, and records that a Nadcap AC7114 auditor can trace from a signed report back to the person. Revision 6 of NAS 410, released in December 2025, is the current one, and customers set the date by which their suppliers' written practices must follow it.

The harbor side runs on SNT-TC-1A

Tank, piping and vessel inspection in the Wilmington and Carson refining district, crane and wharf steel at the Port of Long Beach, and boiler work at coastal power stations follow ASME, API and AWS documents. Those look to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, so the employer's written practice is built on the ASNT document and nobody on the job mentions NAS 410. A technician can hold certifications under both schemes over a career, never under one certificate: each certification names the standard it was issued under.

Crossing from a refinery crew to a rocket factory

  • Your SNT-TC-1A certification ends with your current employer; the new one certifies you again under its own program.
  • The RL3, or the Level 3 who owns the new written practice, decides what earlier training and experience to credit. Keep course outlines, hours and instructor names.
  • Penetrant and magnetic particle are where field technicians usually fall short, because NAS 410 asks for more formal training in those methods than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  • Machined, printed and thin-wall parts need a different eye from weld caps. Penetrant testing training and the Level 2 route cover technique; the employer's procedures and specimens do the rest.
  • Ask whether you will start as a trainee working under direct observation of a certified Level 2 or Level 3, and how long that usually lasts in that shop.
  • Keep a signed experience log split by product form, plus your vision record.

None of that converts an SNT-TC-1A certificate into a NAS 410 one. It gives the next employer evidence to credit.

Atlantis in Long Beach

Launch, aircraft and harbor employers get one Atlantis offer: ASNT NDT Level III consulting, training based on SNT-TC-1A, and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Coursework is self-paced online, with an ASNT NDT Level III on hand for questions and practice in the Practical NDT simulator; the practical itself is done at the employer's facility under its written practice, and no Atlantis classroom exists in Long Beach. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Long Beach employers. Any plan to count outside courses toward a NAS 410 certification needs the RL3's agreement before enrollment. For customer and Nadcap audits, Atlantis prepares NAS 410 audit documentation for the company's RL3 to approve. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A explainer and the Los Angeles page go further.
